hooks.text: Decades of data prove the full moon does not trigger human madness.
Centuries of claiming full moons cause ER chaos are completely unsupported by data.
Over one hundred studies prove full moons have zero impact on human behavior.

title: The Full Moon Myth Busted
description: Decades of data prove the full moon has no effect on human behavior, crime, or emergency room visits.

beats.text: Decades of data prove the full moon does not trigger human madness.
beats.visual: photograph of the full moon seen through a telescope, 2024

beats.text: Police officers and medical staff often blame lunar phases for sudden spikes in emergency room chaos.
beats.visual: photograph of a hospital emergency room entrance at night, 2021

beats.text: Yet meta-analyses of over one hundred studies show zero correlation between the moon and human behavior.
beats.visual: digital illustration of statistical data graphs and lunar phases, 2022

beats.text: Statistical data shows no link to homicide rates, hospital admissions, or human birth rates.
beats.visual: photograph of blue police cruiser lights at a distance at night, 2022

beats.text: The average twenty-eight day human cycle is actually a mathematical mismatch for the twenty-nine point five day lunar month.
beats.visual: infographic comparing the lunar month and human biological cycles, 2023

beats.text: Lunar gravity is far too weak to affect human biology.
beats.visual: photograph of high tide ocean waves crashing against sea cliffs, 2021

beats.text: High tides happen during full moons because the Sun, Earth, and Moon align in space.
beats.visual: diagram showing the gravitational alignment of the Sun, Earth, and Moon, 2022

beats.text: Certain marine species like coral really do sync their spawning cycles with moonlight.
beats.visual: photograph of coral polyps spawning in the ocean at night, 2020

beats.text: While moonlight syncs coral and pulls tides, for human chaos...
beats.visual: photograph of the full moon shining brightly in a dark night sky, 2024
